title: I am black and beautiful — Liber II opens
english: [[I am black and beautiful, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:5]]. The Second Book begins. The Bride speaks to the daughters of Jerusalem — souls still partly carnal. She is black because of penitence, struggles, and the body of humility; beautiful because of the image of God, conversion, and the Bridegroom who loved her. Kedar signifies darkness; Solomon’s curtains, adornment.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Do not look that I am dark; mother’s sons fought me
english: [[Do not look at me because I am dark, for the sun has discolored me >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]. The sun of trials and persecutions sometimes scorches the soul and changes its color, yet does not take away inner beauty. [[My mother’s sons fought against me >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]: those who seemed of the same people or synagogue persecuted the church. [[They made me keeper of the vineyards; my own vineyard I have not kept >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:6]]: while she takes up others’ cares, she sometimes neglects her own.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Tell me where you pasture at noon
english: [[Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you pasture, where you lie down at noon >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:7]]. Noon is full light and perfect knowledge. The Bride does not want to wander among the flocks of companions — heresies and varied teachings — but to find the Word’s pastures at noon itself. If the Bridegroom does not show her, the soul is in danger of going after the tracks of alien flocks.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: If you do not know yourself — pasture goats
english: [[If you do not know yourself, O beautiful among women, go out and follow the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your goats >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:8]]. Knowledge of oneself is the way to God. She who does not know herself pastures among goats, not among sheep; she will not be on the right but on the left. Beautiful among women: the church among synagogues, or the soul among the world’s virtues.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Likened to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots
english: [[I have likened you, my friend, to my cavalry among Pharaoh’s chariots >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:9]]. As far as the Lord’s cavalry differs from Pharaoh’s horses, so far the church from alien daughters. [[Your cheeks are like a turtledove’s; your neck like necklaces >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:10]]. Simplicity and obedience are the soul’s adornment. [[We will make you ornaments of gold studded with silver, while the king is on his couch >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:11-12]]: the Bridegroom’s friends prepare ornaments for a time.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: A bundle of myrrh between my breasts
english: [[A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me; he shall linger between my breasts >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:13]]. Myrrh signifies Christ’s mortification and passion. A bundle: not one drop, but the fullness of the passion. Between the breasts: in the ruling part of the heart, in continual memory, the crucified Christ dwells. As long as we are in this world, we carry the myrrh of the passion between the breasts.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: A cluster of henna in the vineyards of Engedi
english: [[A cluster of henna is my beloved to me in the vineyards of Engedi >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:14]]. Henna is flower and fragrance and medicine; Engedi a place of ointments. Christ is both the fragrance of life and the medicine of wounds and the cluster of new wine. In the vineyards of Engedi: in the churches where the Spirit’s ointments are compounded.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Behold you are beautiful; our couch is shaded
english: [[Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, and fair. Our couch is shaded; the beams of our houses are cedar, our paneling cypress >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:15-17]]. The Bride no longer speaks only of her own blackness, but proclaims the Bridegroom’s beauty. The shaded couch: a soul strewn with flowers of virtues. Cedar and cypress are incorruptible: faith and hope and charity.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: I am the flower of the field; lily among thorns
english: [[I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys. As a lily among thorns, so is my friend among the daughters >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:1-2]]. Christ is the flower that appeared in the field of the world; the lily for the lowly in the valley. The church is a lily among thorns of persecutions and scandals. Thorns prick; the lily keeps its brightness.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Stay me with flowers; his left hand; I adjure you
english: [[Stay me with flowers, heap me with apples, for I languish with love. His left hand under my head, and his right hand will embrace me. I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and stags of the field, not to raise or awaken love until she please >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:5-7]]. Thus far the Second Book has woven its first series of lemmas from I am black through the bundle and the cluster and the couch as far as the adjuration; what follows will come in the next tips.
translator_notes: Liber II after Liber I CLOSEOUT.

title: Behold you are fair; your eyes are doves
english: [[Behold, you are fair, my friend; behold, you are fair; your eyes are doves >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:15]]. The doubled beauty can mark present and future: now fair by imitation of Christ, then fair by perfection itself. Dove-eyes signify spiritual understanding given by the Holy Spirit. Unless the soul receives dove-eyes, she cannot perceive the Word’s beauty.

title: Behold you are fair, my beloved; our couch is shaded
english: [[Behold, you are fair, my beloved, and graceful. Our couch is shaded >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:16]]. Now first the Bride more carefully inspects the Bridegroom’s beauty with those eyes called doves. The shared couch is understood as the soul’s body, in which, while still placed there, she is counted worthy to be taken into partnership with the Word. Shaded: not dry, but wooded with the density of good works.

title: Without dove-eyes the Word seems without beauty
english: Those who only believe, and do not yet have dove-eyes, say of the Word: [[We saw him, and he had no form or comeliness >> Bible:Isaiah 53:2]]. But she who has progressed and received spiritual eyes says: Behold, you are fair. Faith without contemplation hides the form; spiritual understanding reveals the beauty.

title: Cedar beams and cypress paneling — Liber II frame
english: [[The beams of our houses are cedar, our paneling cypress >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:17]]. The soul’s or church’s house is upheld by beams of faith and hope; the paneling is charity. Cedar and cypress are woods that do not rot, because the theological virtues do not decay. These belong to the close of the Second Book, where the Bride speaks no longer only of blackness, but of the adornment of a shared dwelling with the Bridegroom.

title: Historical recapitulation of Book II
english: Historical recapitulation of Book II: the Bride confesses herself black and beautiful; the sun of trials discolors her; her mother’s sons fight her; she is made keeper of vineyards; she asks where he pastures at noon; unless she knows herself she will pasture goats; she is likened to cavalry; the bundle of myrrh and cluster of henna signify the Beloved; mutual beauty and the shaded couch conclude.

title: Spiritual recapitulation of Book II
english: Spiritual recapitulation: blackness of penitence and struggle; beauty of God’s image; sun of persecution; mother’s sons as persecutors from the race; vineyards as churches; noon as perfect knowledge; self-knowledge; goats as the wicked; cavalry of the church against Pharaoh; myrrh of the passion; henna of the Spirit’s ointment; dove-eyes; the couch of a fruitful body.

title: Daughters of Jerusalem as middle souls
english: The daughters of Jerusalem, to whom the Bride speaks, are middle souls: neither wholly carnal nor yet perfect. They are taught through the Bride’s confession not to be scandalized at the church’s blackness in persecutions, but to recognize inner beauty. Book II serves especially for their instruction.

title: Order of love’s ascent in Book II
english: The order of love in Book II: from confession of weakness (I am black) to petition for knowledge (tell me), from self-knowledge to likeness to the divine cavalry, from memory of the passion (myrrh) to praise of the Bridegroom’s beauty. The steps of the advancing soul are marked here.

title: Warning: bridal words need dove-eyes
english: Let the reader beware: the bridal words of Book II are to be understood not carnally, but of the Word and the soul, or of Christ and the church. Whoever lacks dove-eyes remains in the letter and suffers scandal. Whoever has them rests with the Bridegroom in the shaded couch.

title: Liber II CLOSEOUT — toward Liber III
english: End of the Second Book. The Third Book follows, where we shall pursue further the Bridegroom’s beauty and the couch and the flowers of the field. Thus far, from I am black through Our couch is shaded, with the Lord’s help, we have set things in order. Amen.
